finding.description: Describes a defect in the same-role review, not a candidate defect already captured by a supported review finding.

reviewFindingAdjudication.description: Judges one finding made by the same-role review rather than judging the candidate defect again.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain why this review finding is rejected; this array is empty when judgment is supported.

surfaceAdjudication.description: Echoes the bound same-role review assessment in reviewAssessmentJudgment and judges the soundness of that assessment in judgment. A sound blocking review assessment is blocking plus supported, not an adjudication failure.

findingIds.description: Links only adjudicator findings that explain a rejected same-role review assessment. It is empty for supported; rejected requires a linked blocking finding on this surface.

judgment.description: supported approves the same-role review assessment even when reviewAssessmentJudgment is blocking; rejected means the assessment is unsound or incomplete.

reviewAssessmentJudgment.description: Exact echo of the bound same-role review assessment's judgment; the deterministic verifier rejects any mismatch.

adjudicationSchema.description: This record judges the soundness and completeness of the same-role review, not the candidate.

findings.description: Adjudicator findings describe defects in the same-role review's requirement, assessment, reasoning, finding, coverage, or severity; they do not repeat candidate defects already captured by supported review findings.

reviewFindingAdjudications.description: Each entry judges one same-role review finding. A supported review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected review finding requires a linked blocking adjudicator finding that explains the review defect.

surfaceAdjudications.description: Each entry exactly echoes the same-role review assessment's pass, advisory, or blocking judgment, then separately judges that assessment as supported or rejected; it does not judge the candidate surface directly.

verdict.description: pass means the same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate; fail means the same-role review is unsound or incomplete. This verdict never judges the candidate directly.

adjudicationSchema.title: Independent canonical-English semantic adjudication record

adjudicationSemantics.failMeaning: The same-role review is unsound or incomplete.
adjudicationSemantics.findingLinkMeaning: A supported surface assessment or review finding has no adjudicator-finding links; a rejected one links at least one blocking adjudicator finding on an overlapping surface that explains a defect in the review.
adjudicationSemantics.passMeaning: The same-role review is sound and complete, even when that review correctly fails the candidate.
adjudicationSemantics.subject: same-role-review
adjudicationSemantics.surfaceAdjudicationMeaning: Each surface adjudication exactly echoes the bound review assessment judgment in reviewAssessmentJudgment, then uses judgment supported or rejected to judge that assessment.

reviewBundle.inventoryLimitation: This evidence covers only the explicitly declared inventory. Completeness and classification of learner-facing surfaces remain reviewer-judged; the tool does not discover or certify omitted surfaces.
reviewBundle.rubric: Read each routed Rust source card as the learner receives that complete standalone card: caption, accessible label, path, and displayed source excerpt. Judge whether it independently identifies the operation and policy being shown, uses accurate technical English, preserves exact identifiers, and does not depend on hidden ambient context, color, position, or nearby prose to convey its purpose. Report only concrete learner-facing defects; do not edit the candidate or demand stylistic preferences.

surfaces.roleRequirement: The complete standalone source card must identify an explicit non-ambient autograd recording context and show the immutable value plus its recording and no-gradient constructors with an accessible purpose label.
surfaces.value: Choose graph recording explicitly without ambient thread state rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/autograd/tensor_core.rs#autograd-context /// Explicitly selects whether newly created operations record reverse-mode edges. #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct AutogradContext { records_graph: bool, } impl AutogradContext { /// Creates the default training context that records eligible parent edges. pub const fn recording() -> Self { Self { records_graph: true, } } /// Creates an evaluation context that keeps forward checks but records no graph. pub const fn no_grad() -> Self { Self { records_graph: false, } } /// Returns whether operations created with this context may retain parent edges. pub const fn records_graph(self) -> bool { self.records_graph } } impl Default for AutogradContext { fn default() -> Self { Self::recording() } }

surfaces.roleRequirement: The complete standalone source card must state and show that operation creation first checks the forward result, combines explicit context policy with parent tracking to determine the result tracking flag, and removes parent edges for no-gradient execution.
surfaces.value: Check the result, combine context policy with parent state, and omit no-gradient parent edges rust/crates/llm-from-scratch/src/autograd/tensor_core.rs#autograd-operation-policy fn operation_node( context: AutogradContext, value: Tensor, operation: TensorOperation, mut parents: Vec<ParentEdge>, ) -> Result<Self, TensorAutodiffError> { check_finite_forward(&value, operation)?; let tracked = context.records_graph() && parents.iter().any(|edge| edge.parent.tracks_gradient()); if !context.records_graph() { parents.clear(); } Ok(Self::new_node(value, operation, parents, tracked, None)) }

surfaceAssessments.rationale: The purpose label names an explicit choice—graph recording without ambient thread state. The displayed `AutogradContext` has a private `records_graph` value and no mutation operation, while `recording()` and `no_grad()` construct the two states and `records_graph()` reports the selected state, so the standalone card identifies both purpose and policy.
surfaceAssessments.roleRequirement: The complete standalone source card must identify an explicit non-ambient autograd recording context and show the immutable value plus its recording and no-gradient constructors with an accessible purpose label.

surfaceAssessments.rationale: The purpose label states the sequence and policy. In the excerpt, `check_finite_forward(&value, operation)?` precedes policy computation; `tracked` combines `context.records_graph()` with whether any parent `tracks_gradient()`; and `parents.clear()` executes when recording is disabled. Those exact operations independently establish forward checking, combined tracking state, and removal of no-gradient parent edges.
